content_groups.group_title: Q2. What are the common causes?

blocks.text: “Retained products of conception, endometritis and subinvolution of the placental site are major causes. Other causes include coagulopathy, uterine vascular lesions and gestational trophoblastic disease.”

content_groups.group_title: Q3. What is the most important investigation?

blocks.text: “Pelvic ultrasound is an important investigation when retained products or intrauterine pathology is suspected, but investigations should be guided by the clinical presentation.”

content_groups.group_title: Q4. What blood tests would you request?

blocks.text: “FBC, group and crossmatch, coagulation studies, fibrinogen if significant haemorrhage, renal function and other tests such as CRP, lactate and blood gas depending on the clinical condition.”
“Fever, uterine tenderness, offensive lochia and sometimes subinvolution and tachycardia.”
“Failure of the uterus and particularly the placental implantation site to involute at the expected rate after delivery, which can contribute to secondary postpartum haemorrhage.”

content_groups.group_title: Q7. What vascular lesion can cause secondary PPH?

blocks.text: **“A uterine artery pseudoaneurysm or, less commonly, an acquired uterine arteriovenous malformation.”**

content_groups.group_title: Q8. How would you diagnose a uterine artery pseudoaneurysm?

blocks.text: “Colour Doppler ultrasound is an important first-line investigation.”

content_groups.group_title: Q9. How might a pseudoaneurysm be treated?

blocks.text: “Uterine artery embolisation is an important fertility-preserving treatment in appropriate patients, with surgical management considered depending on the clinical situation.”

content_groups.group_title: Q10. What is your immediate priority if she is shocked?

blocks.text: **“Resuscitation and haemorrhage control. I would not delay treatment while waiting for the definitive diagnosis.”**

content_groups.group_title: ❌ Mistake 6: Assuming a normal Hb excludes major bleeding

blocks.text: Acute blood loss may initially have a deceptively normal Hb.
Consider persistent abnormal bleeding where gestational trophoblastic disease is possible.

blocks.title: If you remember only **six things**, remember:

items.text: Think **retained products, infection and subinvolution** first.
**Fever + uterine tenderness + offensive lochia = think endometritis.**
**Recurrent massive bleeding after Caesarean = consider uterine artery pseudoaneurysm.**
**Never blindly instrument a uterus when a vascular lesion is suspected.**

blocks.text: **“In secondary postpartum haemorrhage, I would first assess and stabilise the mother, then determine whether the likely cause is retained products, infection, subinvolution, coagulopathy or a vascular lesion, using clinical assessment, laboratory tests and pelvic imaging to guide definitive treatment.”**
